inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: Instruction says to keep going until every row is complete, with retries and sub agent spawning, and no declared execution limit.
The design relies on the prompt to pursue completion but declares no structural limits on retries, runtime, spend, or delegation.

elements.name: Nightly batch of CRM account rows
Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Max unattended steps and retry ceiling
Hard spend cap or per-run call budget on enrichment API
Structural limit on sub agent depth and count
Spend and quota alerting on enrichment account

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): internal batch can drive unbounded paid enrichment calls and recursive delegation without spend or step limits

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps or retries per account rising, growth in spawned sub agents, or batch size increase; reassess if any hard limit is later added and then changed.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to retry failed lookups and spawn researcher sub agents, then keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call, the nightly batch is 40,000 rows, and about 3 percent of rows are malformed and never return a complete result.
The API key and monthly quota are shared with other teams, so exhaustion causes collateral service loss for sales and marketing.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Enforce a hard per-run call budget and a hard spend cap on cap.enrich_lookup, sized below the shared monthly quota reserve needed by other teams.
Enforce max retries per row, max unattended steps, and bounded runtime; fail rows that exceed the limit instead of continuing indefinitely.
Limit sub agent depth and count and prohibit recursive researcher spawning beyond a fixed depth.
Add spend and quota alerts tied to the shared enrichment account and page operators before the monthly quota is exhausted.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts could not be run in this environment. Present risk is dominated by a property finding under rubric section 5a: consequential spend and delegation capabilities have no hard step, retry, runtime, sub-agent, or spend limits, while malformed rows are known to fail persistently and the prompt requires completion. With A4 autonomy and recursive delegation, the inherent tier rises to critical and no declared or verified control restores the missing property, so residual remains critical. Forecast also remains critical because there are no present controls whose decay would materially worsen the tier; the key reassessment signals are longer task horizon, increased recursion, or any future addition, removal, or weakening of structural limits.

limitations: Assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement.
No runtime configuration, source code, or telemetry was provided, so logging, credential scope enforcement details, and any hidden orchestration controls could not be verified.
No protocol, approval, or quota-management configuration was provided; conclusions about absent structural limits are based on the supplied runtime notes and prompt only.
